Full disclosure I was invited to the show this time around, but the first two times I saw it, I did pay full price out of pocket. So hopefully that is a testament to how much I genuinely really enjoy the show, because whenever anyone asks me what show they should see on Broadway, and Julia is almost always on the list of shows that I give them. Mostly because it's just such a crowd pleaser. Everyone will like it, whether you are a big Broadway fan or someone who has never seen a Broadway show before. And that's because the show is just so fun. It's incredibly funny. I love puns and wordplay, so a lot of the humor in the show is just right up my alley. And even as a certified jukebox musical hater, I actually really like the way that they incorporate the songs in the show. I think it helps that, unlike a lot of other jukebox musicals, they have a wealth of songs from a variety of different artists to choose from. But even other shows that take a similar approach, like Moulin Rouge, do not do it as successfully as an Juliette does, in my opinion. I think a lot of that can be attributed to book writer David West. Read who finds Really clever ways of setting up the songs. There are a lot of lines in the show, and names specifically, that serve to set up punchlines in songs and lyrics further on in the show. They're so subtle that you don't realize that their setups until you get to that song or lyric, and then it's just like, it clicks. It's like, oh, my god, that's so smart. And then, of course, you have this cast LED by Laura Courtney, who is just giving an unreal Broadway debut. Her vocals are insane. I'm obsessed with her performance. I also got to see two new cast members this time around. Charity Angel Dawson, who recently took over the role of nurse, and Austin Scott, who took over the role of Shakespeare a little while ago. I thought they were both great. They're both making the roles their own, doing their own thing, and it helped keep the show fresh for me. So, yeah, if you can't tell, I absolutely loved the show. I'm going to Give it a 4.5 out of five stars. I can't give it the full five stars because there are its fair share of plot contrivances. But it's also. Angela. It's fun, it's camp.
